hypothesis is FALSIFIED by a discriminating three-way test.

  go install github.com/hashicorp/terraform-config-inspect@2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d

B) canary WITH the real binary present and working:
   AssertionError: assert 'abstain' == 'match'
   -> EXACTLY the CI signature (job 101295228786, change 2674; and job 101290520693 on the
      dependabot PR-merged tree).

C) what a missing binary actually does to the corroborator:
   outcome=abstain reason=no_tool reason_detail=executable_not_resolvable
   `_resolve_executable` raises BEFORE any subprocess is spawned, so a missing binary can never
   produce empty stdout and can never raise a JSONDecodeError.

So the CI failure happens WITH a working binary, not without one, and `go install` is not
implicated: its CI step logs ten successful module downloads and no error, and the test's
`has_binary` guard passed (execution reached the assertion at line 429).

ACTUAL REASON, from a direct call against the real binary:
   outcome=abstain  reason=version_skew  reason_detail=config_inspect_schema_skew

The producer contract cannot validate the tool it pins. Validating one real
`terraform-config-inspect --json .` document against terraform_config_inspect.schema.json
yields 15 violations in three classes:
  /: 'required_core' | 'provider_configs' | 'diagnostics' is a required property   (omitempty)
  /*/pos: 'column' is a required property; 'byte' is a required property           (SourcePos
          at the pinned commit is exactly {Filename string, Line int})
  /*/provider: {'name': 'aws'} is not of type 'string', 'null'                     (it is an object)

LATENT SECOND LINK: upstream `dirFiles` builds fullPath = filepath.Join(dir, name), so
pos.filename echoes the directory argument. `_run` passes the ABSOLUTE snapshot path
(terraform_corroborator.py:286), so filenames return absolute and _validate_positions rejects
them at terraform_corroborator.py:367 as path_outside_snapshot. Verified both ways against the
real tool: absolute dir arg -> "filename": "/tmp/realtf/snap/main.tf"; "." -> "filename":
"main.tf". Fixing only the schema would move the abstain, not remove it.

DE-RISKED BEFORE CODIFYING: with the corrected schema plus "." as the directory argument,
applied in a throwaway harness against the real binary:
  variable.region      -> match
  variable.missing     -> abstain no_unique_address
  module.vpc (source)  -> match
  data.aws_ami.base    -> abstain no_unique_address   <- separate defect, filed as eaved-bronze-loris
The first two are exactly the canary's assertions. Dry-running the staged patch on file copies
takes the schema from 15 violations against the real binary to 0.

The test is NOT being softened: it keeps refusing to pass on abstain. The contract is being
corrected to describe the tool that is actually pinned.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py::test_pinned_upstream_canary` fails on the
`optionality / terraform-config-inspect pinned canary` job with
`AssertionError: assert 'abstain' == 'match'`, on changes that are fully up to date with `main`.
Observed on Gerrit change 2674, whose base is `0033662b5534` (current `main`), in
`https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/33961826977/job/101295228786`, and identically on
the dependabot PR-merged tree in job `101290520693`. Rebasing does not help. The job runs on every
patchset, so this blocks the review queue.

`go install` is NOT the cause: its step logs ten successful module downloads and no error, and the
test's own `has_binary` guard passed — execution reached the assertion at line 429. The
discriminating three-way test proving this is recorded as a ticket comment.

## Root cause

The corroborator abstains `config_inspect_schema_skew`. Reproduced locally and deterministically
against the audited binary (`go install
github.com/hashicorp/terraform-config-inspect@2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d`):

```
outcome      : abstain
reason       : version_skew
reason_detail: config_inspect_schema_skew
```

`src/rebar/schemas/terraform_config_inspect.schema.json` is a producer contract that the pinned
tool's output can never satisfy. Validating one real invocation yields 15 violations in three
classes:

1. `pos` requires `column` and `byte`. Upstream `SourcePos` has exactly two fields —
   `Filename string` and `Line int` (`tfconfig/source_pos.go` at the pinned commit).
2. The top-level `required` list demands `required_core`, `provider_configs` and `diagnostics`.
   The tool omits all three when empty, so a clean module never carries them.
3. `resource.provider` is typed `["string", "null"]`. The tool emits an object, `{"name": "aws"}`.

Behind the schema sits a second, latent abstain. `tfconfig/load.go`'s `dirFiles` builds
`fullPath := filepath.Join(dir, name)` and hands that to the parser, so `pos.filename` echoes the
directory argument. `_run` passes the ABSOLUTE snapshot path
(`src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py:286`), so filenames come back absolute, and
`_validate_positions` rejects any absolute filename at
`src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py:367` with `path_outside_snapshot`. Fixing only the
schema would move the abstain, not remove it. Confirmed by running the tool both ways: an absolute
dir argument gives `/tmp/realtf/snap/main.tf`; `.` gives `main.tf`.

The unit suite missed both because it never uses the real tool — `_fixture_binary` builds a fake
whose payload was hand-written, carrying `column`/`byte` fields the tool does not emit. The canary
is the one test that touches reality.

This is a THIRD, independent defect alongside `persuasive-welcome-nymph` (a wall-clock race in the
fault test's own fixture) and `ergophilic-freudian-queenbee` (a CI step failing on pre-gate trees).
Same provenance commit `59d504c2bdbb` / Gerrit 2672, three distinct mechanisms.

## Approach

Correct the producer contract to the tool that is actually pinned, and stop feeding the tool a
path it will echo back:

1. In `terraform_config_inspect.schema.json`, make `pos` require only `filename` and `line`
   (keeping `column`/`byte` as optional properties so a tool revision that adds them still
   validates), drop `required_core`/`provider_configs`/`diagnostics` from the top-level `required`
   list while keeping them as optional properties, and type `resource.provider` as the
   `{name, alias}` object the tool emits, or null.
2. In `_run`, pass `"."` as the directory argument instead of the absolute snapshot path. The
   child's `cwd` is already the snapshot, so this names the same directory, and it makes the tool
   stamp relative `pos.filename`s that `_validate_positions` accepts without relaxing that check
   at all. It also strengthens the existing redaction posture, which already asserts that no argv
   element contains the repo path.
3. Update `test_subprocess_contract_strips_environment_and_copies_readonly_snapshot` to assert the
   new argv contract, and the recorded `invocation.argv` placeholder in `_match_result` to match.

Correcting the schema rather than loosening the abstain is the right shape: the abstain logic is
sound (it refuses to emit T1 evidence it cannot ground), and the canary is correct to refuse a
vacuous pass. The defect is that the contract describes a tool that does not exist.

De-risked before codifying: with exactly these changes applied in a throwaway harness against the
real audited binary, `variable.region` returns MATCH, `variable.missing` returns abstain
`no_unique_address`, and `module_source_equals` on `module.vpc` returns MATCH — the canary's own
assertions, satisfied.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/schemas/terraform_config_inspect.schema.json` — align `pos`, the top-level `required`
  list, and `resource.provider` with the pinned tool's real output.
- `src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py` — pass `"."` as the tool's directory argument in
  `_run`; update the recorded `invocation.argv` placeholder in `_match_result`.
- `tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py` — update the subprocess-contract
  assertions to the new argv, and the fake payload's `pos`/`provider` shape to the tool's real one
  so the fake stops contradicting the schema it is validated against.

## Testing

- RED, reproduced locally: with the audited binary on `PATH`,
  `REBAR_TERRAFORM_CONFIG_INSPECT_CANARY=1 pytest -k pinned_upstream_canary` fails
  `assert 'abstain' == 'match'`, and a direct `corroborate_diagnostic` call reports
  `reason_detail=config_inspect_schema_skew`.
- GREEN, live end-to-end against the real boundary: the same canary command passes with the real
  audited binary installed — the only check that exercises the actual tool.
- Latent-path proof: after the schema fix alone the corroboration still abstains
  `path_outside_snapshot`; after the `"."` change as well it matches, showing both links were
  necessary rather than assuming it.
- Regression: `pytest tests/unit/grounding/ -q` is green and
  `pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py -q` reports the same pass/skip
  counts as before the change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With the audited binary on `PATH`,
      `REBAR_TERRAFORM_CONFIG_INSPECT_CANARY=1 pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py -k pinned_upstream_canary`
      PASSES; recorded as a ticket comment alongside the pre-fix failure text.
      MET — 1 passed, 24 deselected in 13.28s at merged HEAD; pre-fix the same command on the
      same binary gave `assert 'abstain' == 'match'`.
- [x] Validating one real `terraform-config-inspect --json .` document against
      `terraform_config_inspect.schema.json` yields zero violations; verified by a scripted
      `iter_errors` count of 0 (it is 15 today).
      MET — scripted `iter_errors` reports 0 against the merged schema.
- [x] `_run` passes `"."` as the directory argument and the child's `cwd` remains the snapshot;
      verified by the updated subprocess-contract test, which still asserts no argv element
      contains the repo path.
      MET — terraform_corroborator.py:292; test lines 294/295/297; `-k subprocess_contract`
      1 passed.
- [x] Applying only the schema change leaves the corroboration abstaining
      `path_outside_snapshot`, demonstrating the second link was independently necessary;
      recorded as a ticket comment.
      MET — re-run live: corrected schema + absolute dir arg -> abstain/path_outside_snapshot;
      corrected schema + "." -> match.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/grounding/ -q` is green and `make verify` is green before the change is
      pushed to Gerrit.
      MET — 366 passed, 1 skipped at merged HEAD; make verify 19950 passed, 25 skipped, exit 0.

Pass '.' as the tool's directory argument so pos.filename stays relative; update the recorded invocation.argv placeholder.
Update the subprocess-contract argv assertions and the fake payload's pos/provider shape to the tool's real shape.
